FINDING 8 — the new `error[alloc-null]` check (8dd2b7b, 2026-07-28) is defeated
by a one-hop local alias, and the resulting binary really does die on a failed
allocation.

CONTROL (correctly rejected)  alloc_null_check_control_direct.zen.txt
        p := malloc(64)
        b: [i64] := p.slice(1)
        b[0] = 1
CMD:  ./zen check tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/alloc_null_check_control_direct.zen.txt
OUT:  zenc: <file>:5:17: error[alloc-null]: allocation result may be null;
        this dereferences it without checking          rc 1     (correct)

HOLE  alloc_null_check_bypassed_by_alias.zen.txt — the SAME program with one
      extra line, `q := p`:
        p := malloc(64)
        q := p
        b: [i64] := q.slice(1)
        b[0] = 3
CMD:  ./zen check tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/alloc_null_check_bypassed_by_alias.zen.txt
OUT:  zenc: <file>: ok                                 rc 0     (accepted)

AND IT IS NOT THEORETICAL — with the allocation forced to fail:
CMD:  ./zen build tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/alloc_null_check_bypassed_by_alias.zen.txt -o /tmp/an3.bin
      ./scripts/alloc-fuzz/oom-sweep.sh --run /tmp/an3.bin
OUT:  [BUG:NULL] first at FAIL_AT=1  rc=134  :: zen: panic: null pointer dereference
      swept 2 injection points: OK=0 HANDLED=0 BUG=2

`q` is still a bare local in the same function, which is inside the scope the
pass claims ("bare locals only, intraprocedural, body-wide rather than
path-sensitive") — provenance just is not propagated across a local-to-local
binding.

TWO FURTHER MISSES, both explicitly out of the pass's stated scope, so listed
only for completeness (not counted as findings):
  * struct field   `s := S(p: malloc(64))` then `s.p.slice(1)`   -> ok
  * wrapper fn     `mk = () RawPtr<u8> { malloc(64) }`           -> ok

CLASS: false negative in a fresh soundness check (accepts a program that
       segfaults on allocation failure).
FOUND BY: hand-directed probing of the new check, confirmed with
       scripts/alloc-fuzz/oom-sweep.sh --run.
